spec: Given a date string "DD-MM-YYYY" and an integer n (which may be negative), return the date string "DD-MM-YYYY" of the date n days later, correctly handling month and year boundaries and leap years.

Given a date as (year, month, day) integers, a time of day as hour and minute integers (0-23, 0-59), and an integer number of hours n (which may be negative or span multiple days), return a (year, month, day, hour, minute) tuple giving the resulting date and time.

spec: Split the input string on whitespace and count how many times each resulting token appears. Return a dict mapping each distinct token (case-sensitive, punctuation not stripped) to its count. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty dict.
visible_tests: assert word_frequency('the cat sat on the mat') == {'the': 2, 'cat': 1, 'sat': 1, 'on': 1, 'mat': 1}

spec: Count occurrences of each string in items, then return a list of (item, count) tuples for the n most frequent items, sorted by count descending and, for ties, alphabetically ascending. If n exceeds the number of distinct items, return all of them in that order. An empty items list returns an empty list.
Group the strings in words by their length. Return a dict mapping each length to a sorted list of the words that have that length. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a dict whose values are unique and hashable, return a new dict mapping each value to its corresponding key. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Given a dict mapping keys to values where several keys may share the same value, build the reverse mapping: each value maps to a sorted list of all keys that had that value. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Merge two dicts of numbers by summing the values for keys present in both, and keeping the original value for keys present in only one. Return the merged dict; neither input dict is modified. If both inputs are empty, return an empty dict.
Merge two dicts into one containing all keys from both. When a key appears in both, the value from d1 is kept. Return the merged dict without modifying the inputs.
Merge two dicts into one containing all keys from both. When a key appears in both, the value from d2 is kept. Return the merged dict without modifying the inputs.

Merge two dicts whose values are lists. For a key present in both dicts, concatenate d1's list followed by d2's list. For a key present in only one dict, copy its list unchanged. Return a new dict; do not mutate the inputs.
Count how many times each hashable value appears in the list items. Return a dict mapping each distinct value to its count. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a list of 2-element tuples, count how many times each distinct tuple occurs. Return a dict mapping each tuple to its count. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Bucket the integers in nums into fixed-width bins of size bin_size (a positive integer), where a number's bin is identified by its floor-divided lower bound (num // bin_size * bin_size). Return a dict mapping each occupied bin's lower bound to the count of numbers in it. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a sorted list of integer boundaries, assign each number in nums to a bucket index equal to the count of boundaries that are less than or equal to it (so numbers below all boundaries get bucket 0, and numbers at or above the last boundary get the highest bucket index). Return a dict mapping each occupied bucket index to the count of numbers in it. An empty nums list returns an empty dict.
Return a sorted list of the keys that appear in both dicts d1 and d2. If there is no overlap, or either dict is empty, return an empty list.
Return a sorted list of all keys that appear in either dict d1 or d2 (or both). If both dicts are empty, return an empty list.
Return a sorted list of the keys that appear in exactly one of d1 and d2 (not both). If d1 and d2 have identical key sets, or both are empty, return an empty list.

Group the strings in words so that words made of the same multiset of letters (anagrams of each other) end up together. Return a dict mapping the sorted-letters string of each group to a sorted list of the original words in it. An empty list returns an empty dict.

For each word in the list words, count how many of its characters are vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive). Return a dict mapping each word to its vowel count; if a word appears more than once, the entry reflects that word's own count (duplicates just overwrite with the same value). An empty list returns an empty dict.

Return a new dict containing only the key/value pairs from d whose value is greater than or equal to threshold. The original dict is left unmodified. If nothing meets the threshold, return an empty dict.
Return the key in d whose value is the largest. If several keys tie for the largest value, return the smallest such key. The dict is assumed to be non-empty.

For each position in the list items, compute how many times that element has occurred so far, counting the current occurrence (i.e. a running per-value tally). Return a list of these running counts, one per input element, in order. An empty list returns an empty list.

Classify every character of s into one of four categories: 'digits', 'letters', 'spaces', or 'other' (punctuation and everything else). Return a dict with all four keys present, each mapping to the count of characters in that category. An empty string gives all zeros.

Split text on whitespace and count how many words have each length. Return a dict mapping each word length to the number of words with that length. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty dict.

Count occurrences of each distinct value in items. Assign rank 1 to the most frequent value, rank 2 to the next, and so on; when several values are tied on count, break the tie by ordering them alphabetically/numerically (smaller value gets the better, i.e. lower, rank number). Return a dict mapping each distinct value to its rank.

Given a value that is a (possibly nested to any depth) list of lists of integers, flatten it completely and count how many times each integer occurs. Return a dict mapping each distinct integer to its count. An empty list returns an empty dict.

For elements that appear in both list1 and list2, compute the minimum of their counts in each list (like multiset intersection). Return a dict mapping each such shared element to that minimum count; elements missing from either list are excluded. Two empty lists return an empty dict.

Given a dict whose values are integers, count how many keys have an even value and how many have an odd value. Return a dict with keys 'even' and 'odd' mapping to those two counts. An empty dict returns {'even': 0, 'odd': 0}.

Split the integers in nums by parity and sum each group separately. Return a dict with keys 'even' and 'odd' mapping to the sum of the even numbers and the sum of the odd numbers respectively (0 if a group is empty). An empty list returns {'even': 0, 'odd': 0}.

Merge two dicts whose values are lists. For a key present in both dicts, combine both lists into a deduplicated, sorted list of the distinct values. For a key present in only one dict, use a deduplicated, sorted copy of its list. Return the merged dict.
Given a list of words, build a dict mapping each distinct word to a sorted list of the positions (0-based indices) at which it appears in the list. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Count how often each character occurs in s, then return a list of (character, count) tuples for the n most frequent characters, ordered by count descending and, for ties, by character ascending. If n exceeds the number of distinct characters, return all of them. An empty string returns an empty list.

Given a list of dicts with numeric values, compute for each key that appears in at least one dict the average of its values across only the dicts that contain that key. Return a dict mapping each such key to its average (a float). An empty list returns an empty dict.

Count how many times each letter appears in s, treating uppercase and lowercase as the same letter and ignoring any non-letter characters. Return a dict mapping each lowercase letter that occurs to its total count. A string with no letters returns an empty dict.

Group the integers in nums by how many digits their absolute value has (e.g. 0 and -9 both have 1 digit, 100 has 3 digits). Return a dict mapping each digit count to a sorted list of the numbers with that many digits. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a list of candidate names (strings), count how many votes each candidate received. Return a dict mapping each candidate to their vote count. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Split text on whitespace and count how often each adjacent pair of words (a bigram) occurs, using a single space to join the pair into a key like 'word1 word2'. Return a dict mapping each bigram string to its count. A text with fewer than two words returns an empty dict.
visible_tests: assert count_bigrams('the cat sat') == {'the cat': 1, 'cat sat': 1}

spec: Return a sorted list of the keys that appear in both d1 and d2 and map to exactly the same value in each. Keys present in only one dict, or with differing values, are excluded. If there are no such keys, return an empty list.

For every key common to both d1 and d2, compute d1's value minus d2's value. Return a dict mapping each common key to that difference; keys unique to one dict are omitted. If there are no common keys, return an empty dict.
